headline: AI sell-off shows signs of stabilizing as rate-hike odds rise
body: The Nasdaq enters the week sitting roughly 12% below its October record, officially in correction territory after a stretch dominated by selling in AI-infrastructure and chip names. But the latest session showed the first real signs of stabilizing: Micron jumped nearly 6% to lead a bounce in the chip cohort, even as breadth stayed thin elsewhere, with slightly more S&P 500 names falling than rising. That split — a sharp snapback in the names that fell furthest, paired with a flat broader tape — reads as a rotation within the AI trade rather than a wholesale flight from risk. The mood is better described as cautious and searching for a bottom than as either capitulation or renewed conviction.

The more consequential shift this week is in rates. Futures markets have pivoted toward pricing a hike rather than a cut at the December 8-9 Fed meeting, with odds cited as high as roughly 80%, after October payrolls came in near 165,000 versus expectations closer to 65,000. October CPI, due Tuesday, is the next data point traders will use to confirm or unwind that repricing. Earnings from CoreWeave, Rigetti Computing, Cisco, and Applied Materials later this week will be read for whether AI capital-spending plans are holding up. Retail-sentiment trackers showed no sharp new signal today, so this read leans on price action and positioning rather than social chatter.
